captions.linkedin:
The model is getting smarter, and the architecture doesn't have to get bigger.

My view is that many practical AI applications can be built around simpler architectures: well-structured folders, clearly defined prompts, relevant context, and access to the right tools.

More capable models give us an opportunity to spend less effort micromanaging execution and more effort improving context quality, tool interfaces, and result verification.

This does not mean frameworks are becoming obsolete. Their complexity should be justified by measurable improvements in reliability, performance, or maintainability.

The real engineering challenge is determining what the model should decide independently and what the surrounding system must strictly control.

https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents
